title: Perturbation-Level σ8 Suppression via μ(a) < 1: Structural Limits of Scale-Free Modifications
description: This technical note studies a purely perturbation-level, scale-independent modification to the growth equation via μ(a) = 1 − B g(a), with μ < 1 weakening the Poisson source term. Scanning gate amplitude and width while holding μ0 fixed, it finds a universal, geometric doubling of σ8 suppression when broadening the gate from n = 6 to n = 2. Within Planck 1σ on μ0, a scale-free μ(a) closes ~43% of the S8 gap; at ~1.5σ it closes ~73%, implying full resolution requires scale dependence or an additional channel.

growth_equation.description: Modified linear-growth equation (scale-free) where \mu(a) rescales the gravitational source term; f = d\ln D/d\ln a and \tilde{\Omega}_m(a) = \Omega_m a^{-3}/E^2(a).

mu_definition.description: Perturbation-level modification to the effective gravitational coupling (Geff/G); B sets amplitude at fixed gate g(a).

gate_function.description: Sigmoid gate controlling the temporal support of the \mu-modification; n sets steepness and a_t the transition epoch.

calibration.description: Calibration used in n-scans to hold \mu(z=0) = \mu_0 fixed while varying gate width n.

suppression_integral.description: σ8 suppression scales with the temporal support (in \ln a) of the gate, explaining geometric control of growth suppression.

universal_factor_2.description: Central invariant: broadening the sigmoid from n=6 to n=2 doubles σ8 suppression at fixed \mu_0; a geometric property of gate width.

key_results.main_finding: Broadening the gate from n = 6 to n = 2 exactly doubles σ8 suppression at fixed μ0 (2.00 ± 0.01), implying a geometric ceiling: scale-free μ(a) can close ~43% (1σ) to ~73% (~1.5σ) of the S8 gap but cannot fully resolve it.
datasets_used: BOSS DR12 RSD (3 points, full covariance)
Stage-III weak lensing S8 target (S8 ≈ 0.776 ± 0.017) and Planck S8 baseline (0.834 ± 0.016)

sealed_predictions.statement: In a full Boltzmann treatment (CLASS) with scale-free μ(a) and A = 0, the σ8 suppression ratio between n = 2 and n = 6 remains 2.00 ± 0.02 across μ0 ∈ [0.80, 0.95].
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Direct computation of D(a) and σ8 in CLASS or CAMB showing a deviation > 0.02 from the factor-2 ratio when radiation, neutrinos, and ISW/CMB lensing are included.

sealed_predictions.statement: Within Planck 1σ on μ0 (|μ0 − 1| ≤ 0.10), any scale-free μ(a) model cannot close more than ~45% of the S8 gap at fixed Ωm ≈ 0.313.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A joint Planck+RSD+WL analysis demonstrating ≥90% S8 gap closure with a scale-free μ(a) (no k-dependence) while satisfying |μ0 − 1| ≤ 0.10.

kill_criteria: KC1: A full Boltzmann global fit (Planck 2018 TTTEEE+lowE+lensing + BOSS/DESI RSD + WL) shows that the WP1a reference (μ0 ≈ 0.85, n = 2, z_t ≈ 1.01, A = 0, Σ = 1) worsens total χ² by > +10 relative to ΛCDM; this rules out the proposed perturbation channel point.
KC2: The universal factor-2 claim fails in a full solver: Δσ8(n=2)/Δσ8(n=6) deviates from 2.00 by >10% across μ0 ∈ [0.80, 0.95]; this invalidates the geometric invariant central to the paper.

KC3: Under |μ0 − 1| ≤ 0.10, a robust analysis finds that scale-free μ(a) closes ≤20% of the S8 gap (σ8 ≥ 0.807 at Ωm ≈ 0.313), contradicting the reported ~43% ceiling and falsifying the suppression-integral scaling.

KC4: High-precision RSD (e.g., DESI) constrains μ0 ≥ 0.95 at >3σ over 0.3 < z < 1.1, leaving insufficient room for μ < 1 to achieve ≥70% S8 amelioration; this kills the scale-free μ(a) channel as a viable explanation.

KC5: Achieving ≤1σ compatibility with Planck and WL requires introducing more than one additional free parameter beyond μ(a) (e.g., strong k-dependence plus extra time-evolution), violating the stated hard-stop rule and abandoning this EFC pathway.

related_packages.role: Background lemma and motivation; shows background gate cannot suppress σ8 (ΔE^2 ≤ 0).

abstract_short: Perturbation channel μ(a) = 1 − B g(a) with μ < 1 weakens the gravitational source term. Reducing gate steepness from n=6 to n=2 exactly doubles σ₈ suppression (universal factor-2). Within Planck 1σ, scale-free μ(a) closes ~43% of S₈ gap; at ~1.5σ it closes ~73%. Full resolution requires scale dependence or combined channel.

technical_note_I.relationship: Background sign lemma (ΔE² ≤ 0) rules out background channel

A.description: Background amplitude (set to 0 for pure μ-model)

b_sweep.description: Amplitude scan at fixed n=6, A=0

n_sweep.description: Gate width scan at calibrated B, A=0

universal_factor_2.description: Ratio of σ₈ suppression n=2 vs n=6 at fixed μ₀

key_conclusions: Background and perturbation channels are non-degenerate: A controls geometry (Hubble friction), B controls growth (Poisson source term)
Temporal support matters more than instantaneous amplitude: universal factor-2 from gate broadening
Scale-free μ(a) has a structural ceiling: ~43% S₈ closure within Planck 1σ
73% amelioration at ~1.5σ with reference model (μ₀ = 0.85, n = 2)
Full resolution requires scale dependence μ(k,a) or combined channel

data_sources.RSD: BOSS DR12 (3 redshift points, full covariance, Alam+ 2017)

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: Technical Note II establishes a rigorous, geometric ceiling on what a scale-free (k-independent) perturbation-level μ(a)<1 modification can achieve for σ8 suppression: a universal factor-2 doubling when broadening the gate from n=6 to n=2, capping S8 gap closure at ~43% within Planck 1σ and ~73% at ~1.5σ. This simultaneously validates the perturbation channel as a real but insufficient mechanism and proves that full S8 resolution within EFC requires either scale-dependent modifications or an additional channel — directly shaping the WP1b/WP2 development path. It also provides the first controlled RSD χ² comparison against BOSS DR12 for the μ(a) family, anchoring future DESI rapid-response work.

It should be linked to: (a) Technical Note I (10.6084/m9.figshare.31333414) as its direct predecessor, (b) the S8 tension observable node, (c) the BOSS DR12 RSD data node, (d) the sealed fσ8 prediction (32013156), and (e) the EFCLASS theory gap.

The absence of related papers at 1-2 hops suggests the perturbation-channel analysis is genuinely new territory for EFC's graph — creating these edges will expose the critical path from TN-II → EFCLASS solver → DESI rapid-response → KC resolution.
The BOSS DR12 node, once linked, will connect this paper to any future DESI DR2 analyses and the sealed prediction at z=0.7, forming a natural validation chain for the μ(a) family.

implicit_consequences: The ~43% ceiling at Planck 1σ means EFC MUST invoke either k-dependent μ(a,k) or a second channel (e.g., Σ≠1, neutrino coupling, or the combined A+μ interaction) to fully resolve S8 — this is a structural fork point for the programme.

The universal factor-2 invariant is an analytic benchmark: any future EFCLASS Boltzmann run that deviates from 2.00±0.02 on the ratio signals either a bug in the solver or scale-dependent leakage from lensing/ISW — either outcome is informative.

The BOSS DR12 RSD χ² values (Table 1-2) constitute the first EFC-internal RSD confrontation and establish a baseline against which DESI DR2 fσ8 predictions (sealed at 0.430 for z=0.7) can be cross-calibrated when the rapid-response pipeline is assembled.

KC4 of this paper (DESI constraining μ0≥0.95 at >3σ) directly couples to the project's biggest gap: the DESI DR2 rapid-response pipeline. If DESI tightens μ0 that severely, the scale-free channel dies and only k-dependent paths survive.

Technical Note I (background anti-suppression) + Technical Note II (perturbation ceiling) together constitute a complete no-go theorem for the simplest EFC variant: A-only or scale-free-μ-only cannot resolve S8. This should be treated as a foundational result for all downstream work.

The paper's KC5 (hard-stop rule: no more than one extra parameter) implicitly defines EFC's parsimony constraint and will be the benchmark against which any k-dependent extension is judged — if k-dependence requires >1 new free parameter, the programme must justify the complexity or pivot.
